lines.differs: Worse for AtliQ than Trustline NBFC: 60 days to pay instead of 45, and invoicing requires client's written acceptance.
Worse for AtliQ than Al Noor: 60 days to pay instead of 30, and lacks interest on late payments.
Worse for AtliQ than Brightwater: 60 days to pay instead of 45.
Same as Crestline: mutual confidentiality obligations with standard exceptions.
Same as Al Noor: mutual confidentiality obligations with standard exceptions.
Same as Al Noor: mutual confidentiality obligations with standard exceptions.
Same as Orbit Travels: deliverables transfer only upon full payment and AtliQ retains its pre-existing tools.
Same as Crestline: deliverables transfer only upon full payment and AtliQ retains and licenses its pre-existing tools.
Same as PayTrack: deliverables transfer only upon full payment and AtliQ retains and licenses its pre-existing tools.
Worse for AtliQ than Sunrise Foods: liability cap is the entire contract value instead of SOW fees, with uncapped confidentiality and data protection.
Worse for AtliQ than PayTrack: liability cap is the entire contract value instead of SOW fees, with uncapped confidentiality and data protection.
Worse for AtliQ than Rohan Iyer: liability cap is the entire contract value instead of twelve months of fees.
Same as Al Noor: mutual intellectual property indemnities for materials provided by each party.
Better for AtliQ than Acme Retail Group: indemnity is limited to intellectual property infringement rather than covering confidentiality breaches or gross negligence.
Better for AtliQ than Orbit Travels: includes a reciprocal indemnity from the client for materials they supply.
Worse for AtliQ than Acme Retail Group: higher delay penalty (1% of contract value vs 0.5% of milestone fee) and no client-delay carveout.
Better for AtliQ than Brightwater: delay penalty is 1% of contract value per week capped at 10%, instead of 1% per day uncapped.
Worse for AtliQ than Al Noor: delay penalty is calculated on the total contract value instead of only the affected milestone fees.
Same as Al Noor: similar obligations to process data on instructions, restrict international transfers, and notify of breaches.
Better for AtliQ than Trustline NBFC: lacks a strict six-hour breach notification window and client or regulatory audit rights.
Worse for AtliQ than Acme Retail: adds strict local hosting requirements and mandatory breach notification obligations.
Worse for AtliQ than Al Noor: disputes are resolved in Saudi courts under Saudi law instead of the common-law DIFC courts.
Worse for AtliQ than CloudSpan Technologies: disputes are subject to Saudi Arabian courts and law instead of Singapore international arbitration.
Worse for AtliQ than Brightwater: disputes are subject to Saudi Arabian courts and law instead of English courts and law.
